=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:321-323 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The main worker Claude invocation omits `--strict-mcp-config`, allowing project-level MCP servers to load alongside the reviewed server.
  WHY: An unreviewed server loaded from the target checkout can run with worker credentials and expand the execution surface beyond the declared configuration.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:~388 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The smoke deny-rule Claude invocation omits MCP configuration restrictions, allowing project-level MCP servers to load during the test.
  WHY: The smoke test runs in the target checkout with worker credentials available; severity ranges from MAJOR to BLOCKER across reviewers, so the highest severity is used.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:273-278 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The pre-commit guard hook and/or its `claude_pool.py` helper are writable by the worker, allowing the guard to be replaced before committing `.claude/**` changes.
  WHY: The worker can modify files the hook trusts, so the guard can accept protected-path changes; severity ranges from MAJOR to BLOCKER across reviewers, so the highest severity is used.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:278 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The hook is registered with global Git configuration, so it applies to commits outside the target repository.
  WHY: Commits elsewhere on the runner may unexpectedly trigger the target-specific hook; severity ranges from NIT to MAJOR across reviewers, so the highest severity is used.
- scripts/claude_pool.py:twin_guard_violations | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The merge-tree candidate is computed only when `len(merge_heads) == 1`, which the reviewer says causes clean two-parent merges of `.claude/**` to be rejected.
  WHY: In the described merge, the merged file differs from both parent trees, so the guard rejects the commit.
- agents.md:1330 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The claim that the smoke run proves the `commit_guard` and `twin_commit` checks is based on a run predating those checks.
  WHY: The cited run did not execute the later smoke probes, making the stated verification inaccurate.
- scripts/claude_pool.py:_cmd_redact (around line 880 in the new file) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_cmd_redact` reads binary artifacts as text with replacement errors and writes them back as UTF-8, potentially corrupting bytes and preventing secret matching.
  WHY: Binary content may be altered before redaction, leaving the original artifact unrecoverable and the credential unredacted.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:Probe every pool account step (select job), the `if [ "$SECONDS" -ge "$deadline" ]` check inside the probe loop | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The probe loop checks its deadline between probes but does not abort an in-flight probe at the deadline.
  WHY: A probe started just before the deadline can run for its full timeout and consume headroom intended for later select-job steps.
- scripts/claude_pool.py and agents.md:twin_guard_violations / "Work job" contract | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The documentation is described as implying support for octopus merges, which the implementation does not provide.
  WHY: The reviewer says octopus merges that cleanly combine `.claude/**` changes may be rejected even though the documented merge-tree behavior suggests otherwise.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Done: unit tests pass; the runner-repo smoke run succeeds on the wrapper PR's branch; nothing dispatches"
  expected_change_site: A green runner-repo smoke run in `shubhodeep1/claude-workers` against the current PR head (eb3dde7) or a post-review-round-1 head
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: Run 37015227644 predates review round 1 (head 5c32058); later changes added the twin-first commit guard and `commit_guard` / `twin_commit` probes, among other workflow changes, which have not been exercised on a real runner; the wrapper is pinned to `@main` with `[skip ci]`; progress and documentation still mark the condition complete or claim the smoke run proves those checks.
- requirement: agents.md "Work job" contract documents the two-parent merge-tree case as handled by the implementation: "A merge commit may change it only to a merge heads version or, for a two-parent merge, gits own merge of the file (git merge-tree --write-tree)"
  expected_change_site: `scripts/claude_pool.py`, the `if len(merge_heads) == 1 and head:` branch in `twin_guard_violations`
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: The merge-tree candidate is computed only when `len(merge_heads) == 1`; the reviewer says a clean two-parent merge can produce content matching neither parent tree, so the guard rejects it.
- requirement: The documentation should accurately describe the unsupported octopus-merge case, or the implementation should support it.
  expected_change_site: `agents.md` "Work job" contract and `scripts/claude_pool.py` `twin_guard_violations`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The reviewer says the implementation handles a normal two-parent merge but not octopus merges; the docs imply broader merge-tree support.
- requirement: “G6 — Twin-first holds. A worker cannot write the checkout's `.claude/**` through any tool; `workflow-templates/.claude/**` stays writable.”
  expected_change_site: `.github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml`, protected-path enforcement in “Prepare the worker” and “Run Claude”.
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: Deny settings cover Edit, Write, and NotebookEdit, but Bash can write the path; the pre-commit hook only checks ordinary local commits, and `git commit --no-verify` and GitHub MCP pushes bypass it.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml | severity=critical | confidence=5

  WHY: A committed `.mcp.json` can launch additional MCP servers alongside the reviewed GitHub server.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Smoke checks step, the deny-rule `claude -p` invocation (permissions test at approximately line 388) omits both `--strict-mcp-config` and `--mcp-config`.
  WHY: A `.mcp.json` in the smoke checkout can load unreviewed MCP servers during the permissions test with access to worker credentials.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Prepare the worker step, the pre-commit hook installation and `git config --global core.hooksPath "$hooks"` use a worker-writable helper and hook.
  WHY: The worker can replace either with a no-op before committing `.claude/**` changes.
- scripts/claude_pool.py | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `twin_guard_violations`, the `if len(merge_heads) == 1 and head:` branch computing `git merge-tree --write-tree`, reportedly rejects clean two-parent merges of `.claude/**`.
  WHY: The reviewer says the clean merged file differs from both parent trees, causing candidate comparison to fail.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Prepare the worker step, `git config --global core.hooksPath "$hooks"` registers the hook globally rather than only for the target checkout.
  WHY: Commits in other directories can fail unexpectedly if the helper is unavailable or those directories lack `.claude/`.
- Requirement: "Done: unit tests pass; the runner-repo smoke run succeeds on the wrapper PRs branch; nothing dispatches" from docs/implement-plan/claude-actions-worker-pool.md phase 1 checklist and the PR description evidence table.
  Expected change site: A green runner-repo smoke run in shubhodeep1/claude-workers against the current head eb3dde7 or any post-review-round-1 head, exercising the twin-first commit guard pre-commit hook and the commit_guard / twin_commit smoke probes added in review round 7.
  Evidence of absence: Smoke run 37015227644 cited everywhere predates review round 1 (head 5c32058). Seven subsequent rounds rewrote .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml including the core.hooksPath pre-commit hook, the twin-guard subcommand, the commit_guard and twin_commit smoke probes, worker containment, and wrapped-base64 redaction. None of these additions have executed on a real runner. The wrapper is pinned to @main with [skip ci] per AD-6. The agents.md contract claims "The smoke run proves it (check=commit_guard, check=twin_commit)" without live verification.
  severity=high | confidence=5
- Requirement: agents.md "Work job" contract documents the two-parent merge-tree case as handled by the implementation: "A merge commit may change it only to a merge heads version or, for a two-parent merge, gits own merge of the file (git merge-tree --write-tree)"
  Expected change site: scripts/claude_pool.py, the `if len(merge_heads) == 1 and head:` branch in `twin_guard_violations`
  Evidence of absence: The merge-tree candidate is computed only when `len(merge_heads) == 1`; a two-parent merge that cleanly auto-merges `.claude/**` with different changes from both sides produces content matching neither parent tree, so the guard rejects it. Either the contract must be corrected to match the implementation, or the implementation must handle two-parent merges.
  severity=low | confidence=4
